notes.title: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors & Diagonalization
notes.content:
### 1. Fundamental Definition
For any square matrix  \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, non-zero $\mathbf{x}$ is an eigenvector if:
A\mathbf{x} = \lambda\mathbf{x} \implies \det(A - \lambda I) = 0

---

### 2. Cayley-Hamilton Theorem
Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation:
A^2 - \text{tr}(A)A + \det(A)I = \mathbf{0}
